subject: Request: temporary SLA scope exception for multi-region failover (RTO/RPO clarification)
messages:
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@paylake.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Paylake Platform Ops <ops@paylake.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarification on multi-region SLA — Paylake production requirements

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for procurement and our internal risk review, a couple of questions came up around the multi-region failover commitments in the standard SLA. Specifically:

- Our legal team needs clarity on the RTO/RPO targets when failing between regions (primary US-west -> failover US-east). The draft SLA refers to "regionally equivalent availability" but doesn't state specific RTO/RPO windows for cross-region recovery.
- We operate stateful KV caches and a few regional-only downstream connectors. If those connectors cannot be failed over immediately, will Redwood guarantee traffic routing with degraded latency SLAs or is an exception required?

Can you point us to the exact numbers and whether a temporary carve-out/exception is possible while we complete integration testing? We expect procurement to ask for either a quantified cross-region RTO (minutes/hours) or an approved exception.

Attached: high-level diagram of Paylake topology (paylake-topo-v3.pdf)

Best,
Amy
Platform Security Manager
Paylake

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@paylake.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region SLA — Paylake production requirements

Amy —

Thanks for the note. Short answers up front:

- Standard cross-region failover in our hosted tier is treated as a regional disaster event: RTO SLA is 4 hours for traffic restoration to a warm-standby region; RPO is "best-effort" for live session state unless you enable KV replication or use our managed replication addon.
- For downstream connectors that are region-bound we can offer two approaches: 1) a documented SLA exception that preserves the normal latency SLO only in the primary region (we would exclude cross-region latency guarantees until replication is in place), or 2) an accelerated integration plan (our Dedicated/Private customers) to configure data replication and a 90-day validation window to meet cross-region RTO/RPO.

I'll loop in Karthik and Laura to coordinate a formal exception request and the legal language. Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement/legal through the exact wording?

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on multi-region SLA — Paylake production requirements

Team —

I reviewed Paylake's topology (thanks Amy for the diagram). Quick notes for the exception form and the proposed language to legal:

- Proposed exception window: until 2026-05-18 (90 days) Redwood will not be liable for cross-region RTO below 4 hours and will not guarantee cross-region latency targets. We will commit to restoring customer-facing traffic to a warm-standby region within 4 hours of an identified regional outage.
- RPO language: "Best-effort for in-flight session state unless KV replication is enabled; documented snapshots and point-in-time restore windows apply for persisted datasets."
- Operational mitigations: weekly DR runbook tests between the regions during the exception window, an SLA credit schedule if an operational error prolongs recovery beyond 8 hours, and a jointly-signed mutual action plan (MAP) describing tasks for connector replication.

Action items: Rishi to confirm the 4- and 8-hour numbers with Product (I can push a quick internal validation). Laura/Marissa, please prepare the legal exception draft and the SLA appendix that lists the exclusion. Amy — if this sounds acceptable we can share a DocuSign-ready SLA amendment.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@paylake.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region SLA — Paylake production requirements

Rishi / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn. The proposed approach is reasonable from Paylake's perspective as long as:

1) The exception window is documented and timeboxed (90 days is fine).
2) Weekly DR tests are scheduled with Paylake participation and test scope is defined (we want to validate transaction continuity for our settlement service).
3) There is a clear credit formula if restoration crosses 8 hours.

Please send the draft amendment and MAP. We'll run it through Legal and Ops and circle back. Also, sending over a list of the connectors we expect to be regional-only — ops@paylake.com will follow with specifics.

Appreciate the collaborative approach.

—Amy

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Amy Chen <amy.chen@paylake.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on multi-region SLA — Paylake production requirements

Amy —

Attached is our SLA amendment draft (sla-exception-request-form.docx) and the updated DR runbook (redwood-dr-plan-v2.pdf). Key clauses to highlight:

- Exception scope: excludes cross-region latency SLOs and reduces cross-region RTO guarantee to an operational target of 4 hours for traffic restoration to a warm-standby region for the duration 2026-02-20 through 2026-05-20.
- RPO: stated as best-effort for session state; persisted data restores subject to standard recovery point documentation.
- Credit schedule: unilateral credit up to 10% of monthly invoice if a recovery exceeds 8 hours due to Redwood operational fault.
- Test cadence: weekly runbook tests coordinated with Paylake ops; Redwood to provide test results and logs within 24 hours of each test.

Next steps: if Paylake signs off on the 90-day exception and the MAP, we will generate a DocuSign amendment and schedule the first DR test for week of Mar 2nd. If anything needs to be tightened (RTO/RPO shorter windows, larger credits), flag now so we can escalate with Product and Finance.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla-exception-request-form.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document), redwood-dr-plan-v2.pdf (application/pdf)
